questions.coherence: The delta is coherent. It stays in harness code (27 files under scripts/gates, scripts/harness, tests/harness, .harness, .github, .agents, docs/backlog|milestones|harness and AGENTS.md) and closes the three harness rows in the order cp15 set: M18.128, then M18.127, then M18.135. last-ci now has one UNKNOWN code (3) and one ranking (`worst`: red 1 > unknown 3 > wait 2 > 0). Drive, next-task and AGENTS.md all name exit 3. landingBlock became an options object that land.mjs and check-checkpoint both call. Both callers pass parent and proposed backlogs, paths, the commit's ci-evidence.json and a live `ciEvidenceHolds`, so the rule is still written once. HARNESS_PATHS is the single positive list, and docs/harness/README.md cites it instead of restating it. review-content.mjs now owns the digest grammar (parseDigest with `bound:`, parseReviewer, isPosthoc, nextRound, reviewedDiffHash), and review.mjs and check-digest both import it. One drift remains. The reviewer role in the tracked digest now has two spellings for the same kind of reviewer: d0ecbb9 uses `claude:independent-subagent`, and e86cf69 and 742fbdf use `claude:isolated-subagent`. The grammar accepts both, and check-digest enforces neither on new lines (F1).

M18.128: the outer read failure now exits 3, not 0, and so do a failed status query with no completed run and more than LAST_CI_MAX_PENDING pending runs. Each case has a test, including a runs file that is not JSON. M18.127: rounds are counted from the tracked digest; changes-requested lines are kept (live: M18.127 and M18.135 each show r1 changes-requested and then r2 pass, which matches their commit bodies, so cp13 F5 and cp14 F6 are fixed for new commits); rebind lines are checked against the bound pass line and the commit's reviewed diff; check-digest refuses a stale pass the commit added. Its last clause, 'the reviewer field SHALL follow a fixed grammar (`vendor:role[:posthoc]`) that check-digest parses', holds only at the writer. check-digest parses the grammar only to decide posthoc, falls back to the old regex, and accepts a new line with any reviewer string (F1). M18.135 matches cp15's proposed_row word for word. It applies the path-only exemption to every subject (Revert and fixup included). Closing a blocking row, whether by done, removal or unmarking, needs ci-evidence.json at or after the parent, which check-ci-evidence holds live with the new `--since`. Both land.test and checkpoint.test prove the two-step bypass is refused, product paths under scripts/ and docs/ are refused, and a close without evidence, with stale evidence or with forged evidence is refused. No FR row moved, and no requirement was dropped silently.

Live: `check-checkpoint --commit` passes for every commit fd702f1..742fbdf (742fbdf is at 3/8, so cp16 is early). `check-digest --head --full-history` reports '111 M18 task commits have tracked review evidence and Commit cells', exit 0. `last-ci --offline` exits 1, RED ci at fd6b38a. questions.architecture: No package, product contract, SDK, schema or dependency changes. gates.yml gains workflow-level `actions: read` and GH_TOKEN for check-commits, so it can read CI evidence live; the change is read-only and tested in ci-workflow.test. check-ci-evidence gains `--since <sha>`, which is additive and tested. land.mjs and check-checkpoint gain a test-only `--ci-runs-file`. A harness commit can still edit HARNESS_PATHS or ci-evidence's REQUIRED job list and land while the block holds, because both sit on harness paths. That is inherent to self-hosted gates; per-commit review and non-negotiable 2 cover it. No ADR is needed: the landing policy is cited from docs/harness and the M18.123/M18.135 rows.

It closed 3 rows, and M18.140 came from the cp15 record. No FR commit has landed since cp13 (cf3b049). The milestone is bounded by CI capacity, not code. `gh run list --workflow ci.yml --branch main` shows 21 ci runs queued, from 5e59449 (07:57Z) to 742fbdf (17:42Z). bfce2d0's run, in progress at cp15, is queued again. The one run that has completed since cp15 is fd6b38a's 40463451542. Its verify jobs finished by 07:23Z, but its ci-ok aggregator waited until 15:52Z for a runner. findings.evidence: review-content.mjs:136-141: parseReviewer is `^([a-z0-9][a-z0-9.-]*):([a-z0-9][a-z0-9.-]*)(?::(posthoc))?$`, and isPosthoc falls back to /:posthoc\b/ when parsing fails. check-digest.mjs imports only isPosthoc (:17, :114). No check refuses a line whose reviewer fails the grammar. Live: parseReviewer('claude:independent-subagent:m18.139-r2') is null, and isPosthoc('x:y:posthoc-r2') is true. The digest at 742fbdf has d0ecbb9 'claude:independent-subagent' and e86cf69/742fbdf 'claude:isolated-subagent'.
findings.problem: M18.127's clause 'a fixed grammar ... that check-digest parses' is enforced only by review.mjs record, the writer. The remote gate (gates.yml runs check-digest --head --full-history, per M18.119) accepts any reviewer string on a new line. A stream on a worktree based before M18.127, or a hand-appended line, can bring back the ad hoc `...:task-rN` form. A non-grammar suffix such as `:posthoc-r2` is then read as posthoc, and posthocProblems treats posthoc lines differently. The two role spellings for one kind of reviewer show that the field is drifting already.
findings.suggestion: In check-digest, refuse a reviewer field that fails parseReviewer on any digest line that a commit at or after e86cf69 adds. Use the grammar alone, with no fallback, for isPosthoc on those lines, and keep the regex only for older lines. Name one role for the default isolated reviewer in the skill (AGENTS.md already says 'isolated subagent'). Add a digest.test case: an added line 'claude:independent-subagent:m18.200-r2' is refused, and 'x:y:posthoc-r2' is refused rather than read as posthoc.
findings.proposed_row: M18.141 check-digest enforces the reviewer grammar on new lines (cp16 F1) | HARNESS | WHEN check-digest evaluates a digest line added by a commit at or after M18.127's commit THE SYSTEM SHALL refuse a reviewer field that does not match `vendor:role[:posthoc]` and SHALL decide posthoc by that grammar alone (the `:posthoc` regex fallback only for older lines); a harness test SHALL prove an added `claude:independent-subagent:m18.200-r2` line and an added `x:y:posthoc-r2` line are refused, and that pre-grammar lines still pass | M18.127 | todo

findings.problem: The written loop procedure and the practice the gates allow disagree. Read literally, drive forbids the harness rows that cp15 itself ordered. Read loosely, 'red' never stops anything while a blocking row is open. That repeats cp13's lesson: a rule streams read differently needs one meaning. last-ci cannot tell that a pending run is the fix unless a Fixes-ci trailer says so, and the only commit that could say so already landed.
findings.suggestion: Write down one rule in drive step 3 and next-task: while a `blocks-landing` row is open and last-ci exits 1, only that row and commits confined to HARNESS_PATHS may proceed (the same rule landing-block enforces); otherwise exit 1 stops all rows. Or let last-ci print that a blocks-landing row is open, so the operator sees why work continues. Docs-only; no gate change is required, because landing-block already enforces the path rule.
findings.proposed_row: M18.142 drive's red-CI rule agrees with the blocking-row regime (cp16 F2) | HARNESS | WHEN last-ci exits 1 THE SYSTEM's drive and next-task procedures SHALL state one rule: while a `blocks-landing` row is open only that row and commits confined to HARNESS_PATHS may proceed (as landing-block enforces), and otherwise no row starts before the red is fixed; last-ci SHALL name an open `blocks-landing` row in its red output, shown by a harness test | M18.128, M18.135 | todo

findings.problem: This is not a code defect. The human's decision is being made from stale numbers, and M18.135 sharpened the operational consequence: every push, the cp16 record included, moves the tip whose ci run must finish green before M18.117 can close, and adds a run to the back of a queue measured in hours. The red that did complete shows M18.117's known causes from before 14d7ea0's fix, so it says nothing yet about whether the fix works.
